thread:
rachel: heads up
bout the int4 canary (sparrow-lite-int4-v1) we flipped to streaming: we've got a small but consistent class of funcall parse failures (0.7% over last 3k).

diego: example? truncated JSON or malformed fields?

rachel: truncated suffixes mostly, and occasional extra comma before end-of-array. saved one sample:
```
{"action":"send_alert","params":{"msg":"disk near cap","tags":["infra","urgent"],}
```
stream cut before final bracket.

samir: compare to fp16 baseline on same prompts+seed?

rachel: fp16-streaming on same set: 0.03%. int4 batch-mode: 0.09%. so streaming+int4 much worse.

luca: sounds like token framing/chunk boundary chopping. short-term options: 1) add a streaming assembler that buffers until syntactically-closed JSON or TTL; 2) disable retry-on-parse-fail for canary to avoid duplicate tool calls; 3) flip to buffered-mode for payloads > 900 bytes.

diego: also instrument per-chunk CRC and token-index to see where divergence occurs vs fp16. if CRC differs early, it's generation-level.

ci-bot: scheduled: canary/harness/1728507777/run1 (5k)
will post results to /ci/canary/1728507777-report.json.

samir: if generation-level, we'll try 2 quant recipes quickly: (A) per-channel scaling; (B) mixed-precision for last 4 layers. run small grid and collect parse_failure_rate + p95 latency + cost per token.

luca: implement assembler with TTL=150ms for canary; gate only when last-chunk doesn't contain a closing brace/ bracket. latency impact measured on canary should be reported.

rachel: I've paused streaming rollout and enabled buffered fallback. also added a no-retry flag for funcall parser on this model.

diego: once the canary report lands, I'll diff per-token checksums between fp16 and int4 for failing vs passing cases to pinpoint the divergence token index.

ci-bot: report posted: /ci/canary/1728507777-report.json (parse_failure_rate_streaming: 0.71%, buffered: 0.08%, fp16-streaming: 0.03%). checksum-diff median divergence token index: 56 on failing cases.

samir: divergence at token ~56 indicates quant distortion in generation path. next: run per-layer rollback for last-8..last-1 to localize. I'll start a 8-job sweep.

luca: good. keeping the assembler in place until we have a quant fix. thanks team. :thumbsup:
